Strait of Hormuz over the last 24 hours: TACO for the 5th time?

Trump just canceled his own strike again because the Iranians are begging for a deal. Well, if you look at the video from @MarineTraffic, the only visible traffic is through the Iran lane.

At the end of the video, you will see the LNG tanker, Gaslog Shanghai, show up as it was reported that the tanker was abandoned. 

Rotterdam Energy made it through. Lucia A, a Suezmax, made it through at the end of the video using the Oman lane. There are transits happening, but they're not enough to change the oil math.

In my view, unless the US is willing to give Iran complete control over the Strait of Hormuz, there's no deal. That's been the case since the MOU, and it's still the case today.

Now that the Bab al-Mandeb card has been played, I think the next step in escalation is Fujairah. I've been saying that's the last card the Iranians could play, and they've been waiting. No one knows when, but it appears inevitable if they want to force even more concessions from the US.

tweets.full_text:
Reachable node counts are a census of software endpoints, not economic actors. A hobbyist node and a node serving millions via an exchange, custodian, wallet, or payment app are not economically equivalent. Every node is sovereign, but nodes are not equal votes over Bitcoin.

Less than 1% of Bitcoin’s economic weight has adopted BIP-110. The claim that 16%-18% of nodes equals 16%-18% support confuses software distribution with economic consensus. Bitcoin is not one node, one vote.

The public evidence of BIP-110 adoption is concentrated among Knots users and OCEAN/DATUM miners. There is no identified major exchange, custodian, ETF platform, wallet, or payment network enforcing it. More than 99% of Bitcoin’s economic weight has not adopted it.
